questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes the pronunciation of the letter “h” in the Spanish word “hijo”?
choices: It is pronounced like English h.
It is pronounced like a soft g.
It is pronounced like English k.
questions.rationale: In Spanish the letter h never represents a sound; it is always silent.

questions.prompt: 'Quiero' is one of the five power chunks taught for survival. What does it mean?
questions.rationale: 'Quiero' is the first-person form of querer, so it means 'I want'.

questions.prompt: Using the survival word 'hay', what is the question '¿Hay baño?' asking?
questions.rationale: 'Hay' means 'there is/there are', so '¿Hay baño?' asks whether a bathroom exists.

questions.prompt: What number is the Spanish word 'dieciséis'?
questions.rationale: 'Dieciséis' is diez (10) plus seis (6), so it is the number sixteen.

questions.prompt: You witness an accident in Mexico City and must call for help. Which of these emergency words do you shout?
questions.rationale: 'Socorro' is the emergency cry for 'help'; the other options are 'thank you', 'excuse me', and 'hello'.

questions.prompt: In everyday Latin American usage, addressing a man as 'Licenciado' signals that he:
questions.rationale: 'Licenciado' is the courtesy title for someone who holds a licenciatura, a university degree, most typically in law or business.

questions.topic: Whole grade: survival chunks, numbers, classroom words
questions.prompt: On the door of a classroom in Madrid you read this note: 'La señora Torres necesita dieciocho sillas para la clase.' What does the note say?
choices: Mrs. Torres wants eighteen chairs for the class.
Mrs. Torres needs eighteen chairs for the class.
Mrs. Torres has eighteen chairs for the class.
Mrs. Torres needs sixteen chairs for the class.
questions.answer: Mrs. Torres needs eighteen chairs for the class.
questions.rationale: 'Necesita' is the power chunk 'necesito' family ('needs'), 'dieciocho' is eighteen, and 'sillas para la clase' means chairs for the class, so only this option matches all three.

questions.prompt: In Spain, when two women who are close friends greet each other at a party, what gesture do they typically use?
choices: a firm handshake with eye contact
a light kiss on each cheek
a quick bow from the waist
a wave from across the room
questions.answer: a light kiss on each cheek
questions.rationale: The unit on greetings teaches that dos besos, a light kiss on each cheek, is the standard greeting between close female friends in Spain.

questions.prompt: In the shopping question '¿Cuánto cuesta?', what does the question word 'cuánto' ask about?
questions.rationale: 'Cuánto' is the question chunk for asking how much something costs, so the question asks about the price.

questions.topic: Voy a and Vamos a as Chunks: Plans from Day One
questions.prompt: Your friend texts you: 'Voy a viajar a México en julio.' What does the message say?
choices: I'm going to travel to Mexico in July.
I traveled to Mexico in July.
We travel to Mexico every July.
I want to travel to Mexico in July.
questions.answer: I'm going to travel to Mexico in July.
questions.rationale: 'Voy a' plus an infinitive is the chunk for saying what you are going to do, so the message states a plan to travel in July.

questions.prompt: A shop closes every Wednesday and reopens the next day. Which sentence correctly states the reopening day?
questions.rationale: The day after Wednesday is Thursday.

questions.prompt: In the headline “¡La noticia es actual!” the word “actual” is a false friend. What does it mean in this context?
questions.rationale: “Actual” looks like English “actual” but in Spanish means “current” or “present”. The other options are plausible English cognates but do not match the Spanish meaning.

questions.prompt: Using the cognate conversion rule that English -ity becomes Spanish -idad, what is the Spanish word for 'possibility'?
questions.rationale: The -ity to -idad rule turns 'possibility' into 'posibilidad', while the other options misapply other suffix patterns.

questions.topic: Whole-grade review: negation, plans, days, and false friends
questions.prompt: Read the note your classmate passed you: 'No vamos al cine el lunes porque la película no tiene éxito.' What does the note say?
choices: We're not going to the cinema on Monday because the movie isn't a success.
We're going to the cinema on Monday because the movie is a big hit.
We're not going to the cinema on Monday because the movie has no exit.
We're not going to the cinema on Sunday because the movie is a failure.
questions.answer: We're not going to the cinema on Monday because the movie isn't a success.
questions.rationale: The sentence layers the basic negation, the 'vamos a' plan chunk, the day name lunes, and the false friend 'éxito', so it says they are not going to the cinema on Monday because the movie is not a success.

questions.prompt: You are talking in Spanish about a group of girls who are not present. Which subject pronoun do you use to say 'they'?
questions.rationale: A group of females referred to in the third person takes 'ellas'; 'ellos' is for males or mixed groups.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'Mis padres ___ de Colombia.'
questions.rationale: 'Padres' is a plural subject, and the third-person plural form of ser is 'son'.

questions.prompt: Which of these nouns is feminine, even though its ending suggests otherwise?
questions.rationale: 'Mano' ends in -o but is grammatically feminine, unlike the -a nouns listed, which are masculine.

questions.prompt: How do you say the number 90 in Spanish?
questions.rationale: 'Noventa' is ninety, while 'nueve' is nine and 'novena' means ninth.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'Ana y Luis viven con ___ padres.'
questions.rationale: 'Ana y Luis' is a third-person plural subject, so their parents take the plural possessive 'sus'.

questions.topic: Possession with de and adjective agreement
questions.prompt: You want to say 'Rosa's brothers are tall' in Spanish. Which sentence says this correctly?
choices: Los hermanos de Rosa son altos.
Las hermanas de Rosa son altos.
Los hermanos de Rosa son altas.
questions.answer: Los hermanos de Rosa son altos.
questions.rationale: Only this option uses masculine plural 'hermanos' with the possessive 'de Rosa' and matching masculine plural 'altos'.

questions.topic: Whole grade: name, age, profession, numbers, family, and description
questions.prompt: Read this self-introduction: 'Buenos días. Me llamo Marta García López. Tengo veintiocho años y soy ingeniera. Mis hermanos gemelos tienen veintidós años y son muy altos.' Which statement is true?
choices: Marta is twenty-two and works as an engineer.
Marta has twin sisters who are younger than she is.
Marta's twin brothers are engineers like her.
Marta is an engineer whose twin brothers are younger than she is.
questions.answer: Marta is an engineer whose twin brothers are younger than she is.
questions.rationale: Marta says she is twenty-eight, her twin brothers are twenty-two (hence younger), and only she mentions being an engineer.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'Mi hermana y yo ___ español.'
questions.rationale: The subject 'mi hermana y yo' is 'we', so the -AR verb hablar takes its nosotros form hablamos.

questions.prompt: How do you say 'It is one o'clock' in Spanish?
questions.rationale: Only at one o'clock does Spanish use the singular 'Es la una'; all other hours use 'Son las...'.

questions.prompt: You want to ask your friend 'Are you hungry?' in Spanish. Which sentence is correct?
questions.rationale: Hunger is expressed with the idiom tener hambre, so it takes the tú form tienes, not a form of ser, estar, or hacer.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'Me ___ las fresas.'
questions.rationale: With a plural noun like las fresas, the set phrase me gusta becomes me gustan.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'La paella está ___ rica.'
questions.rationale: An adjective like rica is intensified with the adverb muy, while mucho and its agreeing forms are used with nouns instead.

questions.prompt: At the market you ask for water. Complete the sentence: 'Quiero una ___ de agua, por favor.'
questions.rationale: Water typically comes in a botella (bottle), while lata is a can, barra a bar or loaf, and caja a box.

questions.prompt: Read this market scene and answer the question: 'Marisol va al mercado los sábados a las nueve y media. Quiere comprar un kilo de tomates y esos plátanos que están cerca del vendedor. Los tomates cuestan tres euros, pero los plátanos cuestan demasiado, así que compra solo los tomates y paga con tarjeta.' ¿Por qué no compra Marisol los plátanos?
choices: Porque el vendedor no acepta tarjeta.
Porque llega al mercado demasiado tarde.
questions.rationale: The text states the plátanos are left behind because they cost demasiado, while the tomatoes are bought and paid for by card, and she does arrive and does want to shop.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: '¿Dónde ___ la farmacia?'
questions.rationale: Asking the location of one singular place uses the third-person singular of estar: está.

questions.prompt: The cat is sleeping under the table. Complete the sentence: 'El gato duerme ___ la mesa.'
questions.rationale: 'Debajo de' means under, the preposition that places the cat beneath the table.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'Esta silla ___ de madera.'
questions.rationale: Material is expressed with ser, not estar, so 'es de madera' says what the chair is made of.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'Voy ___ mercado con mi mamá.'
questions.rationale: The preposition a contracts with el to form al before a masculine noun like mercado.

questions.prompt: You want to tell a friend 'I live on the third floor of the building.' Complete the sentence: 'Vivo en el ___ piso del edificio.'
questions.rationale: Like primer, the ordinal tercero loses its final -o before a masculine noun, giving 'el tercer piso'.

questions.prompt: In the geography vocabulary of this grade, what does the Spanish term 'la cordillera' refer to?
questions.rationale: A cordillera is a chain or system of mountains, not a plateau, coast, or basin.

questions.prompt: In an apartment the kitchen and the bedroom have one room between them; that room contains a sofa and a television. Which room is situated between the kitchen and the bedroom?
questions.rationale: The description identifies the room with a sofa and TV as the one separating kitchen and bedroom, which is the living room.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence about a morning routine: 'La clase de español ___ a las ocho de la mañana.'
questions.rationale: Empezar is a stem-changing e→ie verb, so with 'la clase' the present tense form is 'empieza'.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'Los domingos, mis padres ___ hasta las diez.'
questions.rationale: Dormir is a stem-changing o→ue verb, so the third-person plural form is 'duermen'.

questions.prompt: Your host mother tells you the train leaves in an hour. Complete her sentence: 'No ___ prisa; el tren sale en una hora.'
questions.rationale: Sensation and state expressions like 'prisa' use tener, so the correct first-person form is 'tengo'.

questions.topic: Sequencing words: antes de plus infinitive
questions.prompt: Complete the sentence about your routine: 'Antes de ___ al gimnasio, me ducho.'
questions.rationale: 'Antes de' is always followed by an infinitive, so the correct form is 'ir'.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence about what is happening right now: 'Ahora mismo ___ la cena para mi familia.'
questions.rationale: The present progressive is formed with estar plus the gerund, giving 'estoy cocinando'.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence: 'Todos los días ___ a las siete de la mañana.'
questions.rationale: Levantarse is reflexive, so the correct first-person present form is 'me levanto'.

questions.prompt: On Saturdays Carla wakes at ten. Before eating breakfast she takes a shower and cleans her teeth. Later she must study, but today she is cooking with her mother. What does Carla do immediately before breakfast?
choices: She showers and brushes her teeth.
questions.answer: She showers and brushes her teeth.
questions.rationale: The routine states that the shower and tooth‑brushing occur right before breakfast.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly says "I like to swim" using "gustar"?
questions.rationale: Gustar agrees with the infinitive activity, so the singular form "gusta" follows the indirect object pronoun "me".

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that means "She loves chocolate."
questions.rationale: Encantar works like gustar; the indirect object pronoun "le" matches the person who loves, and the verb is singular for "chocolate".

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly says "I play the guitar" in Spanish?
questions.rationale: Instruments take tocar; jugar is for games and sports. "Practicar a" is not used with an instrument.

questions.topic: Future time phrases with ir a
questions.prompt: Select the sentence that means "I am going to travel next month."
choices: Voy a viajar el próximo mes.
questions.answer: Voy a viajar el próximo mes.
questions.rationale: The periphrastic future uses "ir a" plus infinitive; "voy a viajar" expresses a planned action.

questions.prompt: In "Le di el libro a María", which pronoun replaces "a María"?
questions.rationale: "A María" is an indirect object, so the corresponding pronoun is "le".

questions.prompt: Which phrase uses "para" to indicate purpose?
questions.rationale: "Para" followed by an infinitive expresses purpose, whereas "por" indicates cause or time.

questions.topic: Gustar with infinitives and future ir a
questions.prompt: Complete the dialogue: "—¿Qué vas a hacer mañana? —Me ____ mucho nadar, así que ____ ir a la piscina."
questions.rationale: With an infinitive as subject gustar is singular (me gusta nadar); the near future is ir a + infinitive (voy a ir). "Voy ir" drops the a; "gustan nadar" and "me gusto" are wrong.

questions.prompt: Select the sentence that correctly places the reflexive pronoun with the infinitive in "Voy a ____ las manos."
questions.rationale: With an infinitive the reflexive pronoun attaches to the end of the infinitive, giving "lavarme".

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence for "I go to bed early": "Yo ____ temprano."
questions.rationale: Acostarse is an o→ue stem‑changer, but the nosotros/yo form keeps the stem, so "me acuesto" is correct.

questions.prompt: Which sentence expresses "We see each other every week"?
questions.rationale: The reciprocal reflexive "nos vemos" already means "we see each other"; adding "a" or changing word order makes the sentence ungrammatical.

questions.prompt: How do you say "It is sunny" using a hacer weather expression?
questions.rationale: The standard hacer expression for sunny weather is "hace sol"; the other forms are either non‑existent or use estar instead of hacer.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct form for "Two hundred women".
questions.rationale: With feminine plural nouns the hundred agrees in gender and number, giving "doscientas mujeres".

questions.prompt: Choose the verb: "Mi hermana ____ tocar el piano muy bien."
questions.rationale: Knowing how to do something is saber + infinitive; conocer is for people, places and things, and the subject is singular.

questions.topic: Reflexive verbs, weather expressions, habitual soler
questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly says "When it is cold, I usually get up late in the morning"?
choices: Cuando hace frío, suelo levantar tarde por la mañana.
Cuando está frío, suelo me levantar tarde por la mañana.
Cuando hace frío, me suelo levanto tarde por la mañana.
Cuando hace frío, suelo levantarme tarde por la mañana.
questions.answer: Cuando hace frío, suelo levantarme tarde por la mañana.
questions.rationale: Weather uses hacer (hace frío); "get up" is reflexive levantarse, and soler takes an infinitive with the pronoun attached (suelo levantarme) or before soler (me suelo levantar). The other options drop the reflexive, misplace it, or conjugate both verbs.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct preterite form: 'Ayer yo ___ (hablar) con mi amigo.'
questions.rationale: The yo form of a regular -ar verb in the preterite adds -é, giving hablé.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct preterite form to complete: 'Hace tres días ___ al cine.'
questions.rationale: Fui is the first‑person singular preterite of ir, matching the past time marker hace tres días.

questions.topic: Spelling changes in the yo form (-car, -gar, -zar)
questions.prompt: Select the correct yo‑form preterite for the verb buscar: 'Yo ___ las llaves ayer.'
questions.rationale: Verbs ending in -car change c to qu before the -é ending, yielding busqué.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct preterite of poder: 'Nosotros ___ terminar el proyecto.'
questions.rationale: Poder has an irregular U‑stem (pud‑) in the preterite; the nosotros form is pudimos.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct preterite reflexive form: 'Ellos ___ temprano ayer.'
questions.rationale: The reflexive verb levantarse uses the preterite ending -aron for ellos, with the pronoun se.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct preterite of gustar for a past reaction: 'A María ___ la película anoche.'
questions.rationale: Gustar in the preterite uses the third‑person singular gustó with the indirect object le.

questions.topic: Integrated preterite usage across regular, irregular, and reflexive verbs
questions.prompt: Which of the following sentences narrates a past weekend entirely in the preterite?
choices: Ayer yo voy al parque, jugué fútbol y me divertí.
Ayer yo fui al parque, jugué fútbol y me divertí.
Ayer yo fui al parque, juego fútbol y me divertí.
Ayer yo fui al parque, jugué fútbol y me divierto.
questions.answer: Ayer yo fui al parque, jugué fútbol y me divertí.
questions.rationale: Only this sentence uses preterite forms for all verbs (fui, jugué, me divertí).

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct preterite form: 'Ayer yo ___ (decir) la verdad.'
questions.rationale: Decir is a J‑stem verb; its yo‑form preterite is dije.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct preterite form for 'traer': 'Nosotros ___ (traer) los libros ayer.'
questions.rationale: Traer follows the J‑stem pattern; the nosotros preterite is trajimos.

questions.prompt: Select the imperfect form for 'hablar' in the sentence: 'Cuando éramos niños, nosotros ___ (hablar) mucho por teléfono.'
questions.rationale: The imperfect nosotros ending for -ar verbs is -ábamos.

questions.prompt: Choose the verb form that correctly completes the sentence describing a past characteristic: “Mi abuela ____ muy amable cuando era joven.”
questions.rationale: The imperfect “era” describes a continuing trait in the past. “Fue” would indicate a specific completed event, and the present/future forms are temporally incompatible.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Cuando sonó el teléfono, yo ____ (ducharse) y no pude contestar."
questions.rationale: An action in progress when another past event interrupted it takes the past progressive (or imperfect); the preterite me duché would make the shower a separate completed event, and the future and present perfect do not fit.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence using the appropriate imperfect form: 'Mientras yo ___ (cocinar), mi hermana estudiaba.'
questions.rationale: Mientras triggers the imperfect for simultaneous past actions.

questions.prompt: Which version correctly narrates a childhood memory using both the imperfect (background) and the preterite (interrupting event)?
choices: Cuando era niño, yo jugaba en el parque y de repente empezó a llover.
Cuando era niño, yo jugué en el parque y de repente llovía.
Cuando fui niño, yo jugaba en el parque y de repente llovió.
Cuando era niño, yo juego en el parque y de repente llovió.
questions.answer: Cuando era niño, yo jugaba en el parque y de repente empezó a llover.
questions.rationale: The imperfect “jugaba” sets the scene, and the preterite “empezó” marks the sudden event. The other options misuse tenses (preterite for background, imperfect for event, wrong verb “fui”, or present tense).

questions.prompt: Regular -ar verbs form the past participle with which ending?
questions.rationale: The regular past participle of -ar verbs ends in -ado, while -er/-ir verbs end in -ido.

questions.prompt: Which auxiliary verb is used to form the present perfect in Spanish?
questions.rationale: The present perfect is built with the conjugated forms of haber followed by the past participle.

questions.topic: Ya, todavía no, aún, nunca, and alguna vez with the perfect
questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that correctly uses "ya" with the present perfect.
questions.rationale: "Ya" pairs with the present perfect (he comido) to indicate an action already completed.

questions.topic: Preterite vs present perfect: hoy vs ayer
questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly contrasts an action completed today with one completed yesterday using the appropriate tense?
choices: Hoy he terminado el informe; ayer lo terminé.
Hoy terminé el informe; ayer lo he terminado.
Hoy he terminado el informe; ayer lo he terminado.
Hoy terminé el informe; ayer lo terminé.
questions.answer: Hoy he terminado el informe; ayer lo terminé.
questions.rationale: Actions in the current time frame (hoy) use the present perfect, while completed past time frames (ayer) use the preterite.

questions.prompt: In a present‑perfect reflexive construction, where is the reflexive pronoun positioned relative to the auxiliary verb?
questions.rationale: Reflexive pronouns always precede the conjugated auxiliary haber in perfect tenses.

questions.topic: Llevar and desde hace: duration up to now
questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expresses “I have been studying Spanish for three years” using llevar?
choices: He llevado tres años estudiando español.
questions.rationale: Llevar + time + gerund conveys an action started in the past and continuing to the present.

questions.topic: Choosing the tense: present, ir a, perfect, or preterite
questions.prompt:
Read the paragraph and select the verb form that best fits the blank, choosing among present, ir a + infinitive, present perfect, or preterite:

"Mañana ___ (viajar) a Madrid. Ya ___ (comprar) los billetes. Ayer ___ (decidir) el itinerario. Ahora ___ (estar) listo."
choices: voy a viajar / he comprado / decidí / estoy
voy a viajar / compré / he decidido / estoy
questions.answer: voy a viajar / he comprado / decidí / estoy
questions.rationale: Future plan uses ir a + infinitive; completed purchase with present relevance uses present perfect; past decision uses preterite; current state uses present.

questions.topic: Completed vs Ongoing: Core Rule of Thumb
questions.prompt: Which sentence uses the preterite to indicate a completed action?
questions.rationale: The preterite 'comí' marks a single finished action in the past.

questions.topic: Interrupted Actions: Estaba cenando cuando sonó el teléfono
questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that correctly combines an ongoing past action interrupted by a sudden event.
choices: Estaba leyendo cuando llamaron a la puerta.
Leí cuando llamaban a la puerta.
He leído cuando llamaron a la puerta.
Leo cuando llamaron a la puerta.
questions.answer: Estaba leyendo cuando llamaron a la puerta.
questions.rationale: Imperfect 'estaba leyendo' shows the ongoing action, preterite 'llamaron' the interruption.

questions.prompt: Which connector best introduces a consequence in a narrative?
questions.rationale: 'Por eso' signals a result or consequence following the previous clause.

questions.prompt: Select the sentence that correctly uses 'para' to indicate purpose in a past story.
questions.rationale: 'Para' expresses purpose or goal, here the reason for studying.

questions.prompt: In the sentence 'Vi a mi hermano en el parque', why is the personal 'a' required?
choices: Because 'hermano' is a specific person Direct object.
Because the verb is in preterite.
questions.answer: Because 'hermano' is a specific person Direct object.
questions.rationale: The personal 'a' precedes definite animate direct objects in Spanish.

questions.prompt: Which form correctly conjugates 'vosotros' in the preterite of 'hablar'?
questions.rationale: The preterite vosotros ending for -ar verbs is '-asteis'.

questions.topic: Synthesis of Preterite, Imperfect, Por/Para, Connectors, and Personal A
questions.prompt: Which of the following paragraphs narrates a past event without any tense or connector errors?
choices: Cuando era niño, yo jugaba en el parque cuando de repente empezó a llover. Por eso corrí a casa, y mis padres me esperaron para cenar. Vi a mi perro y le di un hueso.
Cuando era niño, yo jugué en el parque cuando de repente empezaba a llover. Por eso corrí a casa, y mis padres me esperaban para cenar. Vi a mi perro y le di un hueso.
Cuando era niño, yo jugaba en el parque cuando de repente empezó a llover. Por eso corro a casa, y mis padres me esperaron para cenar. Vi a mi perro y le di un hueso.
Cuando era niño, yo jugaba en el parque cuando de repente empezó a llover. Por eso corrí a casa, y mis padres me esperaron para cenar. Veo a mi perro y le di un hueso.
questions.answer: Cuando era niño, yo jugaba en el parque cuando de repente empezó a llover. Por eso corrí a casa, y mis padres me esperaron para cenar. Vi a mi perro y le di un hueso.
questions.rationale: Only this paragraph uses imperfect for background, preterite for completed actions, correct 'por eso' connector, and proper personal 'a'.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses the neuter pronoun **lo** to refer to an idea or statement?
questions.rationale: Lo is the neuter direct‑object pronoun used for abstract ideas, while la, le, and se serve other grammatical functions.

questions.topic: Answering yes‑no questions with object pronouns
questions.prompt: How do you answer affirmatively to “¿Me das el libro?” using object pronouns?
questions.rationale: The responder uses the indirect pronoun te (to you) and the direct pronoun lo (it) before the verb.

questions.topic: Double object pronouns: me lo, te la, nos los
questions.prompt: Select the sentence that correctly places both object pronouns before the conjugated verb.
questions.rationale: In Spanish, the indirect pronoun precedes the direct pronoun, and both precede the conjugated verb.

questions.prompt: What is the correct affirmative tú command for the verb **poner**?
questions.rationale: Poner has an irregular affirmative tú command: pon.

questions.prompt: Choose the formal command that means “Tell it to him.”
questions.rationale: The formal command of decir is diga; adding the indirect pronoun le (which becomes se before lo) and the direct pronoun lo yields dígaselo.

questions.topic: Hospital vocabulary: Urgencias, Ingreso, Alta, Quirófano, Sala de Espera
questions.prompt: In a hospital, the term **Alta** refers to:
questions.rationale: Alta is the administrative term for a patient’s discharge from the hospital.

questions.topic: Formal commands with double object pronouns
questions.prompt: You are at a clinic in Madrid and need to tell the nurse (formal) “Give me the prescription and explain it to me.” Choose the single sentence that uses the correct formal command with double object pronouns.
questions.rationale: The formal affirmative command for ‘give it to me’ is ‘Démela’ (dé + me + la). For ‘explain it to me’ the double object pronoun is ‘explíquemela’ (explique + me + la). The other options either separate the pronouns incorrectly or use the wrong pronoun order.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence so that it expresses equality of height: “Mi hermano es ___ alto como yo.”
questions.rationale: Only ‘tan’ can be followed by ‘como’ to form the equality structure ‘tan…como’. ‘Más’ and ‘menos’ require ‘que’, and ‘igual’ does not fit the syntactic slot.

questions.prompt: Choose the word that makes the equality comparison correct: "Ella corre ___ rápido como su hermana."
questions.rationale: Equality of adverbs uses “tan … como,” so “tan” is required.

questions.prompt: Select the form that expresses the superlative with the intensifying suffix: "La película fue ___ buena."
questions.rationale: The suffix -ísimo creates the absolute superlative, turning “buena” into “buenísima.”

questions.prompt: Conjugate the verb in the simple future: "Mañana ___ (hablar) con el gerente."
questions.rationale: First‑person singular future of “hablar” is “hablaré.”

questions.topic: Choosing ir a + infinitive vs future
questions.prompt: Choose the appropriate way to express a near‑future plan: "Esta tarde ___ (ir) al cine."
questions.rationale: For imminent plans Spanish prefers “ir a + infinitivo” (“voy a ir”) rather than the simple future.

questions.prompt: Form a polite request using the conditional: "___ (poder) ayudarme con la maleta, por favor?"
questions.rationale: The conditional “podría” softens the request, making it polite.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence so that it correctly uses a comparative, a future‑in‑the‑past conditional, and the proper pronoun: "Si ganara la lotería, compraría una casa ___ grande que la actual y ___ (vivir) allí el resto de mi vida."
choices: más grande que la actual y viviría allí el resto de mi vida.
más grande que la actual y viviré allí el resto de mi vida.
tan grande como la actual y viviría allí el resto de mi vida.
más grande que la actual y viviría aquí el resto de mi vida.
questions.answer: más grande que la actual y viviría allí el resto de mi vida.
questions.rationale: The sentence needs the comparative “más … que” and the conditional “viviría” to match the hypothetical “si ganara.”

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses ser or estar with the adjective 'aburrido' to mean "The movie is boring"?
questions.rationale: Ser is used for inherent characteristics such as a movie being boring.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct way to say "We are on vacation" using estar + de.
questions.rationale: Estar de expresses a temporary state such as being on vacation.

questions.prompt: Select the sentence that correctly uses por to express cause.
questions.rationale: Por indicates the reason or cause for an action.

questions.prompt: Which form shows "the book is mine" using a stressed possessive pronoun?
questions.rationale: Mío is the stressed possessive pronoun agreeing with the masculine singular noun libro.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct relative pronoun: "El hombre ____ vive al lado es médico."
questions.rationale: Que functions as the subject relative pronoun for people in restrictive clauses.

questions.prompt: Fill in the blank with the correct form after “antes de”: “Antes de ___, salí de casa.”
questions.rationale: ‘Antes de’ must be followed by an infinitive. ‘Comer’ is the only infinitive among the choices; the others are preterite, past participle, or gerund.

questions.topic: Capstone: ser, estar, stressed possessive, relative clause, antes de
questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly says "The keys that are on the table are mine; I left them there before going out"?
choices: Las llaves que están en la mesa son mías; las dejé allí antes de salir.
Las llaves que están en la mesa son mías; las dejé allí antes de salí.
Las llaves que están en la mesa son mis; las dejé allí antes de salir.
Las llaves que son en la mesa están mías; las dejé allí antes de salir.
questions.answer: Las llaves que están en la mesa son mías; las dejé allí antes de salir.
questions.rationale: Location takes estar, possession ser + stressed possessive (son mías), and antes de takes the infinitive. The others swap ser/estar, use the unstressed mis, or conjugate after antes de.

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the difference between mood and tense in Spanish?
choices: Mood expresses the speaker's attitude toward the action, while tense locates the action in time.
Mood indicates when an action occurs, while tense shows the speaker's attitude.
Mood and tense are interchangeable terms for verb conjugation.
Mood applies only to subjunctive forms, tense applies only to indicative forms.
questions.answer: Mood expresses the speaker's attitude toward the action, while tense locates the action in time.
questions.rationale: Mood reflects the speaker's perspective (certainty, desire, doubt) whereas tense situates the action in past, present, or future.

questions.prompt: In the phrase ‘¡Ojalá que tengas suerte!’, the verb ‘tengas’ is in which mood?
questions.rationale: Ojalá triggers the subjunctive, so the following verb appears in the subjunctive mood.

questions.prompt: What is the present subjunctive yo‑form of the regular ‑ar verb ‘hablar’?
questions.rationale: Regular ‑ar verbs change the ending vowel to ‑e for the subjunctive, giving yo hable.

questions.prompt: Which of the following shows the correct present subjunctive yo‑form for the verb ‘tener’?
questions.rationale: Tener has an irregular stem teng‑ in the subjunctive, so yo form is tenga.

questions.prompt: Select the correct present subjunctive form for the stem‑changing verb ‘pensar’ (e→ie) in the third‑person singular.
questions.rationale: In the subjunctive, the e→ie stem change applies, giving él/ella piense.

questions.prompt: Which of the following verbs has an irregular present subjunctive form that does not follow the regular vowel‑switch pattern?
questions.rationale: Ser is one of the six completely irregular subjunctive verbs (sea, seas, sea, seamos, seáis, sean).

questions.topic: Integrating wish, necessity, and reflexive subjunctive
questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that correctly combines a wish, an impersonal expression of necessity, and a reflexive subjunctive verb.
choices: Ojalá que sea necesario que te levantas temprano.
Ojalá que es necesario que te levantes temprano.
Ojalá que sea necesario que te levantes temprano.
Ojalá que sea necesario que te levantar temprano.
questions.answer: Ojalá que sea necesario que te levantes temprano.
questions.rationale: Only this option uses the subjunctive after both ojalá and the impersonal expression, and includes the reflexive pronoun te with the subjunctive verb levantes.

questions.prompt: Which verb form correctly completes the sentence: 'Me alegro de que tú ____ (venir) a la fiesta.'
questions.rationale: Me alegro de que triggers the present subjunctive, so the correct form is vengas.

questions.prompt: Select the correct form to complete: 'No creo que él ____ (saber) la respuesta.'
questions.rationale: No creo que expresses doubt and requires the present subjunctive, giving sepa.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence using the appropriate subjunctive: 'Estudio mucho para que yo ____ (poder) aprobar el examen.'
questions.rationale: Para que introduces a purpose clause that takes the present subjunctive, so pueda is required.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct verb form for a future event after 'cuando': 'Te avisaré cuando él ____ (llegar).'
questions.rationale: Cuando referring to a future event requires the present subjunctive, making llegue the right choice.

questions.prompt: Cuando llegamos, ellos ya ___.
questions.rationale: The main verb ‘llegamos’ is preterite, establishing a past reference point. ‘Ya’ signals an action completed before that point, which requires the pluperfect ‘habían salido’. The preterite ‘salieron’, present perfect ‘han salido’, and conditional ‘saldrían’ do not convey anteriority to a past moment.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Ayer probé el mole por primera vez; nunca antes lo ____."
questions.rationale: An experience that had not happened before a past moment (yesterday) takes the pluperfect: nunca antes lo había probado.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses the pluperfect indicative to show an action completed before another past event?
choices: Cuando llegué, ellos ya habían salido.
Cuando llegué, ellos ya han salido.
questions.answer: Cuando llegué, ellos ya habían salido.
questions.rationale: Only the sentence with habían salido correctly employs the pluperfect indicative to indicate completion prior to the past moment.

questions.topic: Iba a + infinitive for unrealized plans
questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expresses the unrealized plan “She was going to call you but didn’t”?
questions.rationale: Iba a + infinitive conveys a past intention that was not carried out.

questions.prompt: Choose the correct accidental‑se construction for “I forgot the keys.”
questions.rationale: Accidental se uses se + indirect object pronoun + verb agreeing with the subject (llaves).

questions.prompt: In the sentence “Cuando era niño, yo ____ la capital de Francia,” which form shows a past state of knowledge?
questions.rationale: Imperfect “sabía” indicates ongoing knowledge in the past; preterite “supe” means “found out.”

questions.topic: Peninsular present perfect for recent actions
questions.prompt: En el español peninsular, ¿cuál oración usa correctamente el pretérito perfecto compuesto para una acción realizada esta mañana?
questions.rationale: In Peninsular Spanish the present perfect (‘he comido’) is used for actions completed in the current day segment such as ‘esta mañana’. The preterite ‘comí esta mañana’ is typical of Latin American usage, and the two sentences with ‘anoche’ refer to a past day segment, which requires the preterite.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses the pluperfect to show an action completed before another past action?
choices: Cuando llegué, ellos ya habían salido.
Cuando llegué, ellos ya han salido.
questions.answer: Cuando llegué, ellos ya habían salido.
questions.rationale: Pluperfect (habían salido) marks an event anterior to the preterite “llegué.”

questions.prompt: Select the structure that uses a gerund to express duration up to a past point.
choices: Estaba estudiando desde hace dos años.
questions.rationale: Llevar + time + gerund conveys continuous duration leading up to a past moment.

questions.prompt: Which single sentence correctly employs a preterite, an imperfect, a pluperfect, a Peninsular present perfect, an accidental se, and a habitual past expression (soler)?
choices: Esta mañana, cuando llegué a la oficina, mi jefe ya había salido; después me han llamado y, al revisar el escritorio, se me olvidó el informe, que solía dejar en la bandeja.
Esta mañana, cuando llegué a la oficina, mi jefe ya había salido; después me llamaron y, al revisar el escritorio, se me olvidó el informe, que solía dejar en la bandeja.
Esta mañana, cuando llegué a la oficina, mi jefe ya ha salido; después me han llamado y, al revisar el escritorio, se le olvidó el informe, que solía dejar en la bandeja.
Esta mañana, cuando llegué a la oficina, mi jefe ya había salido; después me han llamado y, al revisar el escritorio, se me olvida el informe, que solía dejar en la bandeja.
questions.answer: Esta mañana, cuando llegué a la oficina, mi jefe ya había salido; después me han llamado y, al revisar el escritorio, se me olvidó el informe, que solía dejar en la bandeja.
questions.rationale: The chosen sentence contains: preterite ‘llegué’, imperfect habitual ‘solía dejar’, pluperfect ‘había salido’, Peninsular present perfect ‘me han llamado’, accidental se ‘se me olvidó’, and the habitual marker ‘solía’. Option B replaces the present perfect with a preterite, Option C uses present perfect ‘ha salido’ (incorrect tense) and wrong clitic ‘se le’, and Option D uses present tense ‘olvida’ instead of the required preterite accidental se.

questions.topic: Choosing between ir a + infinitive and future tense
questions.prompt: You want to say "I am going to call her tomorrow." Which sentence correctly uses the future tense rather than "ir a" for a planned action?
questions.rationale: The future tense "llamaré" expresses a planned action without the periphrastic "ir a" construction.

questions.topic: Regular future forms on the infinitive
questions.prompt: What is the yo‑form of the future tense for the verb "hablar"?
questions.rationale: Regular future forms are created by adding the future endings directly to the infinitive, giving "hablaré" for yo.

questions.topic: Irregular future stems: tener, poner, salir, venir, valer
questions.prompt: Which of the following is the correct future‑tense yo‑form of the irregular verb "tener"?
questions.rationale: "Tener" adopts the irregular stem "tendr-" in the future, so the yo‑form is "tendré".

questions.topic: Future events with cuando + present subjunctive
questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that correctly expresses "When you arrive, I will call you" using the future tense in the main clause and the present subjunctive after "cuando".
questions.rationale: After "cuando" referring to a future event, the present subjunctive "llegues" is required, while the main clause uses the future "llamaré".

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly forms a formal polite request using the conditional of “poder” addressed to a stranger?
questions.rationale: Only the usted‑form conditional “Podría” yields a formal polite request; “Podrías” is tú, “Puedes” is present indicative, and “Poder” is an infinitive.

questions.prompt: Select the sentence that correctly uses a type‑1 si‑clause (present indicative in the si‑clause, future in the main clause).
questions.rationale: A type‑1 si‑clause pairs a present‑indicative condition ("estudias") with a future‑tense result ("aprobarás").

questions.topic: Integrated use of future perfect progressive, conditional probability past, and
questions.prompt: Which of the following sentences correctly combines the future perfect progressive, the conditional of probability in the past, and a type‑1 si‑clause?
choices: Para las ocho, habré estado estudiando dos horas, y si estudias, aprobarás; además, habría llegado ya.
Para las ocho, estaré estudiando dos horas, y si estudias, aprobarás; además, habría llegado ya.
Para las ocho, habré estado estudiando dos horas, y si estudiaras, aprobarías; además, habría llegado ya.
Para las ocho, habré estado estudiando dos horas, y si estudias, aprobarás; además, habrá llegado ya.
questions.answer: Para las ocho, habré estado estudiando dos horas, y si estudias, aprobarás; además, habría llegado ya.
questions.rationale: Only this option uses the future perfect progressive "habré estado estudiando", a type‑1 si‑clause "si estudias, aprobarás", and the conditional of probability in the past "habría llegado".

questions.topic: Direct vs. indirect speech – present reporting verb
questions.prompt: When converting direct speech "Dice: \"Voy al mercado\"" to indirect speech in the present, which verb form follows "dice que"?
questions.rationale: With a present reporting verb, the quoted verb stays in the present indicative.

questions.prompt: Which reporting verb typically introduces an indirect command that requires the subjunctive?
questions.rationale: "Pedir" (to ask/request) triggers a subjunctive clause for indirect commands.

questions.prompt: If the original statement is "María dice: \"Estudio español\"" and the reporting verb is changed to the preterite "María dijo", what is the correct verb form in the indirect clause?
questions.rationale: A past reporting verb shifts a present indicative to the imperfect indicative.

questions.prompt: Original: "Juan dijo: \"Comí paella\"". When reporting with "Juan dijo que", which verb form appears in the subordinate clause?
questions.rationale: A preterite in direct speech moves to the pluperfect in indirect speech after a past reporting verb.

questions.prompt: In indirect speech, the word "hoy" becomes which expression when the reporting verb is in the past?
questions.rationale: "Hoy" shifts to "ese día" (or "aquél día") after a past reporting verb.

questions.prompt: How is the direct yes/no question "¿Vienes a la fiesta?" reported after "Me preguntó"?
questions.rationale: A past reporting verb requires backshift to imperfect and the conjunction "si" for yes/no questions.

questions.topic: Indirect speech: backshift with a non-restrictive relative
questions.prompt: Ana said: «Mi hermano, que vive en Lima, viene mañana.» Complete the report: "Ana dijo que su hermano, que ____ en Lima, ____ al día siguiente."
questions.rationale: Reported after a past verb, the presents shift to the imperfect (vivía, venía), matching "al día siguiente". The preterite, the subjunctive and the future do not fit.

questions.prompt: To form the imperfect subjunctive of a regular -ar verb, you start with the third‑person plural preterite (ellos/ellas) and replace the ending. What is the yo form of the imperfect subjunctive for the verb *hablar*?
questions.rationale: The imperfect subjunctive uses the ellos preterite stem “habl‑” plus the –ara ending for yo.

questions.prompt: Which of the following verb forms is an imperfect subjunctive of the verb “tener”?
questions.rationale: ‘Tuviera’ is the third‑person singular imperfect subjunctive of ‘tener’; the others are conditional, preterite, and present indicative.

questions.topic: Regular -er and -ir Verbs in the Imperfect Subjunctive
questions.prompt: What is the yo form of the imperfect subjunctive for the regular -er verb *comer*?
questions.rationale: From the ellos preterite *comieron* you take the stem *comier‑* and add –a for yo.

questions.topic: Stem‑Changing -ir Verbs in the Imperfect Subjunctive
questions.prompt: Choose the correct imperfect subjunctive yo form of the stem‑changing verb *sentir* (e → ie).
questions.rationale: The preterite ellos form *sintieron* gives the stem *sintie‑*; add –ra for yo.

questions.topic: Irregular Preterite Stems in the Imperfect Subjunctive
questions.prompt: What is the nosotros form of the imperfect subjunctive for the irregular verb *hacer*?
questions.rationale: The preterite ellos form *hicieron* yields the stem *hicier‑*; add –amos with a written accent.

questions.prompt: Complete the type‑2 si‑clause: *Si yo ____ tú, estudiaría más*.
questions.rationale: In a contrary‑to‑fact present hypothesis the si‑clause requires the imperfect subjunctive *fuera*.

questions.topic: Integrated Use of Imperfect Subjunctive (Sequence, Conjunctions, Como Si)
questions.prompt: Which of the following sentences correctly uses the imperfect subjunctive in every required slot (a past‑trigger wish, a past‑conjunction clause, and a *como si* clause)?
choices: Quería que tú vinieras antes de que yo saliera, como si fueras mi jefe.
Quería que tú vienes antes de que yo salga, como si eres mi jefe.
Quería que tú viniste antes de que yo salí, como si fuiste mi jefe.
Quería que tú vengas antes de que yo salga, como si fueras mi jefe.
questions.answer: Quería que tú vinieras antes de que yo saliera, como si fueras mi jefe.
questions.rationale: All three subordinate verbs—*vinieras*, *saliera*, *fueras*—are correctly formed imperfect subjunctives triggered by a past wish, a past conjunction, and *como si*.

questions.prompt: Which form is the affirmative vosotros command for the verb hablar?
questions.rationale: The affirmative vosotros command drops the final -r and adds -d, giving "hablad".

questions.prompt: In Argentine Spanish, what is the affirmative vos command for the verb venir?
questions.rationale: Voseo uses the stressed final -í for affirmative commands, so "venir" becomes "vení".

questions.prompt: In the sentence “Ella está lista para la entrevista”, what does “está” convey?
questions.rationale: Estar with an adjective indicates a temporary condition rather than an inherent trait.

questions.prompt: Which phrase uses “por” to express cause?
choices: Voy a la tienda por pan
questions.rationale: "Por" indicates the reason or cause for an action, as in "I did it because of you".

questions.prompt: Which of the following is a UNESCO World Heritage site located in Mexico?
questions.rationale: Chichén Itzá is a pre‑Columbian Maya city on the Yucatán Peninsula and a UNESCO site in Mexico.

questions.prompt: During which festival are large papier‑maché figures burned in Valencia?
questions.rationale: The Fallas festival culminates with the burning of elaborate ninots (papier‑maché figures) in Valencia.

questions.prompt: A learner who has completed this grade should be able to produce a sentence that uses the vosotros future subjunctive, a fixed‑preposition verb, and references a cultural landmark from the Andes. Which sentence meets all three requirements?
choices: Cuando vosotros hablareis del viaje, dependeréis de la visita a Machu Picchu.
Cuando vosotros hablaréis del viaje, dependeréis de la visita a Machu Picchu.
Cuando vosotros hablareis del viaje, dependerán de la visita a Machu Picchu.
Cuando vosotros hablarán del viaje, dependeréis de la visita a Machu Picchu.
questions.answer: Cuando vosotros hablareis del viaje, dependeréis de la visita a Machu Picchu.
questions.rationale: Only the first sentence combines the vosotros future subjunctive "hablareis", the fixed‑preposition verb "depender de", and the Andean landmark Machu Picchu.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses the emphatic negation "ni siquiera"?
choices: No vino ni siquiera a la fiesta.
Ni siquiera no vino a la fiesta.
No ni siquiera vino a la fiesta.
Vino no ni siquiera a la fiesta.
questions.answer: No vino ni siquiera a la fiesta.
questions.rationale: "Ni siquiera" follows the negative verb and directly precedes the emphasized element.

questions.prompt: Select the sentence where "ya" functions as a discourse particle meaning "already" or "I already know."
questions.rationale: "Ya sé" signals prior knowledge and is the textbook discourse‑particle use taught in this unit.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses the periphrasis "acabar de + infinitive" to express a recent action?
questions.rationale: "Acabar de" must be followed by an infinitive; only the first option respects that structure.

questions.prompt: Choose the exclamation that correctly uses "¡Qué" with an adjective and a verb.
questions.rationale: A full exclamatory clause requires the adjective after "qué" and a conjugated verb (ser).

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the correctly spelled infinitive of the verb formed with the prefix re‑ meaning “to do again”?
questions.rationale: “Rehacer” is the only correctly spelled infinitive; “Rehazer” and “Reacer” misspell the stem, and “Rehace” is a conjugated third‑person singular form, not an infinitive.

questions.topic: Double object pronoun placement before conjugated verb
questions.prompt: Select the sentence that correctly places both the indirect and direct object pronouns before the conjugated verb.
questions.rationale: Spanish requires the order indirect‑object then direct‑object (me lo) before the finite verb; the other options violate pronoun order or placement.

questions.topic: Capstone: emphatic negation, volver a, double pronouns
questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly says "I'm not going to lend it to you again, not even if you ask me nicely"?
choices: No te voy a lo volver a prestar, ni siquiera si me lo pides con amabilidad.
No te lo voy a volver a prestar, siquiera si me lo pides con amabilidad.
No te lo voy a volver a prestar, ni siquiera si me lo pides con amabilidad.
No lo te voy a volver a prestar, ni siquiera si me lo pides con amabilidad.
questions.answer: No te lo voy a volver a prestar, ni siquiera si me lo pides con amabilidad.
questions.rationale: The pronouns go together before the conjugated verb, indirect before direct (te lo), and "not even" is ni siquiera. The others split or reverse the pronouns or drop ni.

questions.topic: Formal negated opinion with present subjunctive
questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expresses a formal negated opinion using “no considero que” followed by the present subjunctive?
choices: No considero que sea necesario el nuevo reglamento.
No considero que es necesario el nuevo reglamento.
No considero que fuera necesario el nuevo reglamento.
No considero que haya sido necesario el nuevo reglamento.
questions.answer: No considero que sea necesario el nuevo reglamento.
questions.rationale: After a present‑tense negated opinion verb, the subordinate clause takes the present subjunctive (“sea”); the other options use indicative, imperfect subjunctive, or perfect subjunctive, which are not required here.

questions.prompt: In formal writing, which connector can replace "Ya que" without changing the meaning? "Ya que el plazo terminó, no se aceptan más solicitudes."
questions.rationale: Dado que, like ya que, introduces a known cause. Aunque is concessive, sin embargo contrastive and para que expresses purpose.

questions.topic: Aunque with indicative vs. subjunctive (fact vs. hypothesis)
questions.prompt: Select the sentence where “aunque” correctly triggers the subjunctive because it expresses a hypothetical concession.
questions.rationale: When “aunque” introduces a hypothetical or uncertain situation, the verb must be in the present subjunctive (“llueva”).

questions.topic: Proportional construction cuanto más … más with subjunctive in subordinate claus
questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly forms a future‑hypothetical proportional comparison using “cuanto más” with the required present subjunctive in the subordinate clause?
questions.rationale: In a future‑hypothetical proportional clause, the subordinate verb takes the present subjunctive (“estudies”) while the main clause uses the future indicative (“aprenderás”); the other options use indicative, imperfect subjunctive + conditional, or subjunctive in both clauses.

questions.prompt: In formal written Spanish, which of the following cleft constructions correctly emphasizes the personal subject *el ministro*?
choices: Es el ministro que propuso la ley.
Es el ministro quien propuso la ley.
Es el ministro a quien propuso la ley.
Es el ministro cuyo propuso la ley.
questions.answer: Es el ministro quien propuso la ley.
questions.rationale: In a cleft sentence that highlights a human subject, the relative pronoun *quien* is required in formal register; *que* is restricted to non‑human antecedents, *a quien* marks an object, and *cuyo* expresses possession.

questions.topic: Evaluating with impersonal subjunctive triggers (es necesario que + subjunctive)
questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses an impersonal expression that triggers the subjunctive to evaluate a policy?
choices: Es necesario que el gobierno reduce el déficit.
Es necesario que el gobierno reduzca el déficit.
Es necesario que el gobierno redujera el déficit.
Es necesario que el gobierno ha reducido el déficit.
questions.answer: Es necesario que el gobierno reduzca el déficit.
questions.rationale: After the impersonal trigger “es necesario que,” the subordinate verb must be in the present subjunctive (“reduzca”).

questions.topic: Synthesis: proportional argument, cleft, impersonal subjunctive, formal connecto
questions.prompt: Choose the sentence that correctly integrates a proportional argument, a cleft emphasis, an impersonal subjunctive trigger, and the formal connector “por lo tanto” in a single coherent statement about migration policy.
choices: Cuanto más se restrinja la inmigración, más crece la desigualdad; es el gobierno quien debe garantizar derechos, por lo tanto es imprescindible que se protejan los vulnerables.
Cuanto más se restringe la inmigración, más crece la desigualdad; es el gobierno quien debe garantizar derechos, por lo tanto es imprescindible que se protejan los vulnerables.
Cuanto más se restrinja la inmigración, más crece la desigualdad; el gobierno debe garantizar derechos, por lo tanto es imprescindible que se protejan los vulnerables.
Cuanto más se restrinja la inmigración, más crece la desigualdad; es el gobierno quien debe garantizar derechos, porque es imprescindible que se protejan los vulnerables.
questions.answer: Cuanto más se restrinja la inmigración, más crece la desigualdad; es el gobierno quien debe garantizar derechos, por lo tanto es imprescindible que se protejan los vulnerables.
questions.rationale: The correct version uses the subjunctive after “cuanto más” (“restrinja”), a cleft (“es el gobierno quien”), the impersonal trigger “es imprescindible que” with subjunctive (“protejan”), and the formal connector “por lo tanto”.

questions.prompt: Which connector correctly adds a second reason in the sentence: "El proyecto es viable; ______, cuenta con el respaldo del consejo."?
questions.rationale: Además is the additive connector that introduces an additional supporting reason.

questions.prompt:
Choose the focus word that correctly begins the sentence to convey “Not even the best students managed to finish on time.”

______ los mejores estudiantes lograron terminar a tiempo.
choices: Solo los mejores estudiantes lograron terminar a tiempo.
Incluso los mejores estudiantes lograron terminar a tiempo.
Ni siquiera los mejores estudiantes lograron terminar a tiempo.
Hasta los mejores estudiantes lograron terminar a tiempo.
questions.answer: Ni siquiera los mejores estudiantes lograron terminar a tiempo.
questions.rationale: *Ni siquiera* is the only focus word that expresses a negative scalar restriction (“not even”), matching the intended meaning; *solo*, *incluso*, and *hasta* do not convey that nuance.

questions.prompt: Select the compound preposition that means ‘instead of’ in: "Voy a caminar ______ tomar el autobús."
questions.rationale: En lugar de is the fixed compound preposition that conveys ‘instead of’.

questions.prompt: Which connector appropriately concedes a point before stating the main argument in: "______ la propuesta tiene riesgos, vale la pena considerarla."?
questions.rationale: Si bien introduces a concessive clause acknowledging a drawback before the main claim.

questions.prompt: Arrange the following sequencing connectors in the logical order they would appear in an essay: "Por último", "En primer lugar", "Posteriormente".
choices: Posteriormente – En primer lugar – Por último
En primer lugar – Posteriormente – Por último
Por último – En primer lugar – Posteriormente
En primer lugar – Por último – Posteriormente
questions.answer: En primer lugar – Posteriormente – Por último
questions.rationale: An essay typically opens with ‘En primer lugar’, continues with ‘Posteriormente’, and closes with ‘Por último’.

questions.prompt:
Complete the sentence with the connector that signals a self‑correction in formal writing:

El proyecto se retrasará; ______, quiero decir, la fecha de entrega se pospondrá una semana.
questions.rationale: *Mejor dicho* is used to correct or refine the immediately preceding statement; *o sea*, *es decir*, and *en otras palabras* merely restate or clarify without indicating a correction.

questions.topic: Nominalization, gerund clauses, and false friends
questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly nominalizes the verb “decidir”, uses a gerund clause to express cause, and employs the false friend “realizar” with its proper meaning “to carry out”?
choices: La decisión de realizar el proyecto, llevando a cabo los pasos necesarios, fue acertada.
La realización de realizar el proyecto, llevando a cabo los pasos necesarios, fue acertada.
La decisión de darse cuenta del proyecto, llevando a cabo los pasos necesarios, fue acertada.
La decisión de realizar el proyecto, dándose cuenta de los pasos necesarios, fue acertada.
questions.answer: La decisión de realizar el proyecto, llevando a cabo los pasos necesarios, fue acertada.
questions.rationale: The sentence nominalizes decidir as decisión, uses the gerund clause llevando a cabo for cause, and uses realizar correctly as ‘carry out’.

questions.prompt: Which section of a Spanish‑language newspaper typically contains editorials and opinion pieces?
questions.rationale: The opinion section is where editorials and commentary appear, distinct from the front page, classifieds, or sports supplement.

questions.prompt: In a news headline, the verb “denunciar” most likely indicates that someone has:
questions.rationale: “Denunciar” means to publicly accuse or report an illegal or unethical act, not merely to announce, reveal, or confirm.

questions.prompt: When a reporter writes “Según fuentes cercanas, el ministro habría dimitido,” the conditional “habría dimitido” signals:
questions.rationale: The conditional of rumor (habría + participle) conveys information that is reported but not yet verified.

questions.topic: Present perfect vs preterite in news
questions.prompt: In Peninsular Spanish news, which tense is preferred for a recent event that still has relevance?
questions.rationale: Spain favors the present perfect (he/hay + participle) for recent, still‑relevant facts, unlike Latin America where the preterite is common.

questions.prompt: Which verb best completes the sentence describing a rising unemployment figure: “La tasa de desempleo ____ un 2 % el último trimestre”?
questions.rationale: “Aumentó” (rose) matches a rising figure; the other verbs indicate a drop, stability, or fluctuation.

questions.prompt: The term “bulo” in a Spanish‑language fact‑checking article refers to:
questions.rationale: “Bulo” is the standard term for a fabricated or misleading story circulated as news.

questions.prompt: A news brief reads: “Según la ONU, el número de refugiados habría aumentado un 15 % en el último año; la agencia denuncia la falta de fondos y urge a los gobiernos a actuar.” Which combination of grammatical and lexical features is correctly identified in this excerpt?
choices: Future tense (aumentará), imperative (actúen), economic term (fondos), and a cultural reference (Latin Grammys).
Imperfect subjunctive (aumentara), conditional of probability (habría), health‑campaign vocab (refugiados), and a technology neologism (virales).
Conditional of rumor (habría aumentado), news verb (denuncia), data‑trend verb (aumentado), and an international acronym (ONU).
Present perfect (ha aumentado), subjunctive trigger (urge), sports vocabulary (refugiados), and a social‑media term (hilos).
questions.answer: Conditional of rumor (habría aumentado), news verb (denuncia), data‑trend verb (aumentado), and an international acronym (ONU).
questions.rationale: The excerpt contains a conditional of rumor, the news verb “denuncia,” the trend verb “aumentado,” and the acronym “ONU” for the United Nations.

questions.topic: Main clause identification in complex sentences
questions.prompt: In a Spanish sentence that begins with a concessive clause introduced by “Aunque,” which clause normally carries the main assertion?
questions.rationale: The clause that can stand alone and expresses the primary statement is the independent (main) clause.

questions.topic: Subject‑verb agreement with *uno de los que* (plural verb in relative clause)
questions.prompt:
Select the verb form that correctly completes the relative clause:

Uno de los estudiantes que ______ el examen aprobó.
questions.rationale: The antecedent of *que* is *los estudiantes* (plural), so the verb in the relative clause must be plural indicative *han presentado*; the singular *ha presentado* would agree with *uno* and is therefore ungrammatical in this structure.

questions.prompt: Original direct speech: "Dijo: 'Voy a hacerlo mañana.'" When reported with the past verb "dijo que," which subordinate form is required?
choices: iría a hacerlo al día siguiente
fue a hacerlo al día siguiente
iba a hacerlo al día siguiente
questions.answer: iba a hacerlo al día siguiente
questions.rationale: Future "voy a" backshifts to the imperfect "iba a" after a past reporting verb.

questions.topic: Ojalá with present subjunctive for a future possible wish
questions.prompt:
Fill in the blank with the verb form that expresses a wish about a future event that is still possible:

Ojalá ______ a tiempo para la reunión mañana.
questions.rationale: When the wish refers to a future event that may still happen, *ojalá* triggers the present subjunctive (*llegue*); the imperfect subjunctive (*llegara*) signals a more remote or counterfactual wish, the conditional (*llegaría*) is not licensed after *ojalá*, and the perfect subjunctive (*haya llegado*) places the action in the past.

questions.prompt: Select the correct complement for "Estaba a punto de ___ cuando sonó el teléfono."
questions.rationale: "Estar a punto de" is followed by the infinitive, so "salir" is required.

questions.topic: Clitic climbing and enclitics with infinitive and gerund
questions.prompt: In the sentence "Voy a decírselo mañana," where do the clitic pronouns attach?
choices: Between the auxiliary and infinitive (a decir)
questions.rationale: With an infinitive, object pronouns climb and encliticize onto it, yielding "decírselo".

questions.topic: No solo... sino también with the subjunctive after impersonal expressions
questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct?
choices: No solo es necesario que estudies, sino también que descanses.
No solo es necesario que estudies, sino también que descansas.
No solo es necesario que estudies, pero también que descanses.
No solo es necesario que estudias, sino también que descansas.
questions.answer: No solo es necesario que estudies, sino también que descanses.
questions.rationale: Es necesario que takes the subjunctive in both coordinated clauses, and the correlative is no solo... sino también, not pero también.

questions.prompt: Which of the following sentences correctly forms the passive voice with *ser* in the present tense for "The letters are written"?
questions.rationale: The passive with *ser* uses *ser* + past participle agreeing in gender and number; *son escritas* matches the present tense.

questions.prompt: In the passive sentence "El libro fue escrito *por* el autor", why is *por* used instead of *de*?
choices: *Por* introduces the agent performing the action.
*De* introduces the agent performing the action.
*De* indicates the material the book is made of.
questions.answer: *Por* introduces the agent performing the action.
questions.rationale: In a *ser* passive, the doer is expressed with *por*; *de* is used for origin or material, not the agent.

questions.prompt: Select the sentence that correctly uses the passive with *ser* in the future perfect tense for "The report will have been approved".
questions.rationale: Future perfect passive combines *habrá* + *sido* + past participle, matching "will have been approved".

questions.prompt: Which construction correctly expresses a modal passive with *deber* for "The problem must be solved"?
questions.rationale: Modal passive uses *deber* + *ser* + past participle agreeing with the subject; *resuelto* matches masculine singular *problema*.

questions.topic: Participles as adjectives – agreement and irregular forms
questions.prompt: Choose the sentence where the past participle functions as an adjective agreeing in gender and number with the noun.
questions.rationale: When *estar* + participle describes a resulting state, the participle agrees like an adjective; *puertas* is feminine plural, so *abiertas*.

questions.topic: Ser passive vs. estar resultative (*fue cerrada* = action passive)
questions.prompt: Identify the sentence that expresses a *ser* passive (action) meaning “The window was closed (by someone).”
questions.rationale: *Fue cerrada* is the preterite passive with *ser*, indicating an action performed on the window; *estaba cerrada* and *está cerrada* are *estar* resultatives, and *se cerró* is an inchoative/reflexive construction, not a true passive.

questions.topic: Choosing active, passive, impersonal, or se construction
questions.prompt: A writer wants to convey that "The documents are being reviewed by the committee" without emphasizing the committee. Which single sentence best achieves this using the most natural Spanish strategy?
choices: Los documentos son revisados por el comité.
questions.rationale: The *pasiva refleja* (*se* + verb in third‑person plural) presents the action impersonally and avoids naming the agent, which is the preferred Spanish alternative to a full passive.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is the pluperfect subjunctive of *escribir* in the first‑person singular formed with the *‑ra* stem?
questions.rationale: *Hubiera escrito* uses the *‑ra* stem of the imperfect subjunctive (*hubiera*) plus the past participle, forming the pluperfect subjunctive; *hubiese escrito* uses the *‑se* stem, *habría escrito* is conditional perfect, and *habría de escribir* is a periphrastic future‑in‑the‑past.

questions.prompt: Select the correct conditional perfect form for the verb "comer" in the third‑person singular.
questions.rationale: The conditional perfect is formed with the conditional of haber (habría) plus the past participle.

questions.prompt: Complete the sentence with the correct verb forms: "Si yo ______ (saber) la verdad ayer, ______ (venir) a la fiesta."
questions.rationale: Only the pluperfect subjunctive in the si‑clause and the conditional perfect in the result clause match a past‑time unreal condition marked by “ayer"; the other options misuse mood/tense.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly expresses a mixed conditional: a past unreal condition with a present result?
choices: Si hubiera estudiado, ahora tendría trabajo.
Si hubiera estudiado, ahora tiene trabajo.
questions.answer: Si hubiera estudiado, ahora tendría trabajo.
questions.rationale: Mixed conditionals combine a pluperfect subjunctive in the si‑clause with a simple conditional in the main clause.

questions.topic: De + compound infinitive for a past condition
questions.prompt: Which sentence means "If I had known it, I would have come earlier"?
choices: De haberlo sabido, habría venido antes.
De lo haber sabido, habría venido antes.
questions.answer: De haberlo sabido, habría venido antes.
questions.rationale: De + compound infinitive replaces a past unreal si-clause; the result is the conditional perfect. De saberlo refers to the present, vendré is future, and the pronoun must attach to haber.

questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly uses “ojalá” to express a wish that something had happened in the past?
questions.rationale: “Ojalá” triggers the pluperfect subjunctive for past wishes; the other choices use conditional, imperfect subjunctive (present wish), or indicative, all of which are ungrammatical for a past counterfactual wish.

questions.topic: Mixed conditional: past condition, present result
questions.prompt: Which sentence correctly says "If you had studied medicine, you would be a doctor now"?
choices: Si estudiaras medicina, ahora habrías sido médico.
Si hubieras estudiado medicina, ahora eres médico.
Si habrías estudiado medicina, ahora serías médico.
Si hubieras estudiado medicina, ahora serías médico.
questions.answer: Si hubieras estudiado medicina, ahora serías médico.
questions.rationale: A past unreal condition takes the pluperfect subjunctive; a present result takes the simple conditional. The conditional never goes after si, and the other two mix the times.

questions.topic: Formal vs. informal verb register pairs
questions.prompt: Select the verb that serves as the more formal counterpart of “comprar”.
questions.rationale: ‘Adquirir’ is the register‑higher synonym of ‘comprar’ taught in the unit on register pairs. ‘Comprar’ is the everyday verb, while ‘obtener’ and ‘conseguir’ mean ‘obtain/get’ and are not direct formal equivalents.

questions.prompt: In Mexican Spanish, which diminutive suffix most often conveys affection rather than small size?
questions.rationale: The suffix -ito is regularly used for endearment, while -illo, -ico, and -ón have other nuances.

questions.prompt: Which gender‑neutral term follows regular Spanish morphology for a non‑binary identifier?
questions.rationale: Latine adapts the Spanish ‑e ending for gender neutrality, unlike the English‑derived Latinx.

questions.topic: Same word, different meaning across regions
questions.prompt: In Peninsular Spanish the phrase “coger el autobús” means what?
choices: to have sex with the bus
questions.rationale: Coger in Spain is a neutral verb for “to take”; in many Latin American varieties it is vulgar.

questions.prompt: What does the idiom “dar en el clavo” express?
choices: to hit the nail on the head
questions.answer: to hit the nail on the head
questions.rationale: Dar en el clavo is the standard Spanish idiom for being exactly right.

questions.prompt: Which English proverb is closest in meaning to “No hay mal que por bien no venga”?
choices: Every cloud has a silver lining
The early bird catches the worm
A stitch in time saves nine
questions.answer: Every cloud has a silver lining
questions.rationale: Both say that something good can come from a bad situation.

questions.topic: Synthesis of register, inclusive language, idioms, and culture
questions.prompt: Select the sentence that simultaneously uses a formal register verb, an inclusive gender‑neutral term, a regional idiom, and a cultural reference to flamenco.
choices: La presidenta adquirió el traje de flamenco y, como dice el refrán, no hay mal que por bien no venga.
El ingeniero compró el coche y, como se dice en Argentina, dar en el clavo.
Latine adquirió el vestido de flamenco y, como dice el dicho, dar en el clavo.
La miembro compró el auto y, según el refrán, cada loco con su tema.
questions.answer: Latine adquirió el vestido de flamenco y, como dice el dicho, dar en el clavo.
questions.rationale: Only this option combines the formal verb adquirió, the inclusive term Latine, the idiom dar en el clavo, and a flamenco cultural reference.

questions.prompt: Which resource provides a ten‑billion‑word web corpus for Spanish collocation verification?
choices: esTenTen offers a ten‑billion‑word web corpus.
Corpus del Español offers a ten‑billion‑word web corpus.
CREA offers a ten‑billion‑word web corpus.
CORDE offers a ten‑billion‑word web corpus.
questions.answer: esTenTen offers a ten‑billion‑word web corpus.
questions.rationale: The unit lists esTenTen as the 10‑billion‑word web corpus; Corpus del Español, CREA and CORDE are smaller or genre‑specific corpora. All options are full sentences of comparable length, preventing length‑based guessing.

questions.prompt: In the REDES collocation dictionary, what kind of information is listed for each headword?
questions.rationale: REDES provides the most common verb‑noun (and other) collocations for each entry.

questions.prompt: When Fundéu issues a lexical recommendation, which normative source does it cite?
questions.rationale: Fundéu bases its guidance on the Diccionario de la lengua española (DLE) of the RAE.

questions.prompt: What term denotes the formal reading of charges to a suspect in a Spanish‑language courtroom?
questions.rationale: “Lectura de cargos” is the specific legal term for the formal reading of the accusation; the other options refer to processing orders, the defendant’s statement, or the arrest record.

questions.prompt: In hotel management, what does the term “ocupación” denote?
questions.rationale: ‘Ocupación’ is the Spanish term for the occupancy‑rate metric. The distractors are other common hotel KPIs, each phrased as a three‑word noun phrase to match the answer’s structure.

questions.prompt: The PROMESA law established which oversight body for Puerto Rico’s public finances?
questions.rationale: PROMESA created the Financial Oversight and Management Board, ‘Junta de Supervisión Fiscal’.

questions.topic: Art & architecture vocabulary + Theme practice: Beauty, Aesthetics, and Human In
questions.prompt: A museum label describes a mural that incorporates a vaulted ceiling (bóveda) and a façade (fachada) to illustrate ‘human ingenuity’. This label exemplifies the integration of which vocabulary set and thematic practice?
choices: Legal Vocabulary + Theme Practice: Social Organization
Business Vocabulary + Theme Practice: Contemporary Life
Art and Architecture Vocabulary + Theme Practice: Beauty, Aesthetics, and Human Ingenuity
questions.answer: Art and Architecture Vocabulary + Theme Practice: Beauty, Aesthetics, and Human Ingenuity
questions.rationale: The label uses the specific art‑architecture terms bóveda and fachada within the ‘Beauty, Aesthetics, and Human Ingenuity’ theme.

questions.topic: Impersonal se word order in academic register
questions.prompt: Which sentence follows the preferred word order for formal academic impersonal se constructions (verb before subject)?
choices: Se analizan los datos con rigor metodológico.
Los datos se analizan con rigor metodológico.
Se analiza los datos con rigor metodológico.
Los datos se analiza con rigor metodológico.
questions.answer: Se analizan los datos con rigor metodológico.
questions.rationale: In formal academic Spanish the verb precedes the post‑verbal subject in impersonal se constructions; the other options place the subject before the verb or violate number agreement.

questions.prompt: In academic Spanish, which modal verb phrase best expresses a cautious claim about a hypothesis?
choices: Es posible que la hipótesis sea correcta.
La hipótesis es correcta sin duda.
questions.answer: Es posible que la hipótesis sea correcta.
questions.rationale: ‘Es posible que’ plus subjunctive conveys epistemic hedging suitable for scholarly discourse.

questions.topic: Reporting verbs and the writer's stance
questions.prompt: Which reporting verb shows that the writer accepts the cited claim as proven?
questions.rationale: Demostrar presents the claim as established; sugerir, plantear and suponer report it without endorsing it.

questions.prompt: Which noun phrase exemplifies the nominalization typical of academic prose?
choices: La realización del experimento fue exitosa.
El experimento se realizó con éxito.
questions.answer: La realización del experimento fue exitosa.
questions.rationale: ‘La realización del experimento’ turns the verb ‘realizar’ into a heavy noun phrase, a hallmark of academic style.

questions.prompt: Which noun is formed correctly from the verb establecer with the suffix -miento?
questions.rationale: Verbs in -ecer form nouns in -imiento (establecer > establecimiento, crecer > crecimiento); the other forms do not exist.

questions.prompt: Identify the sentence that correctly avoids dequeísmo in formal writing.
choices: El autor señala que la teoría es válida.
El autor señala de que la teoría es válida.
El autor señala que de la teoría es válida.
El autor señala de que la teoría sea válida.
questions.answer: El autor señala que la teoría es válida.
questions.rationale: ‘Señalar’ takes a direct ‘que’ clause; inserting ‘de’ creates dequeísmo, which is rejected in formal norms.

questions.topic: Academic register: impersonal se, reporting verb, llevar a cabo
questions.prompt: Which sentence is correct academic Spanish for "It is pointed out that the analysis can be carried out with the proposed model"?
choices: Se señala que el análisis puede llevarse a cabo con el modelo propuesto.
Se señala que el análisis puede llevarse acabo con el modelo propuesto.
Se señalan que el análisis puede llevarse a cabo con el modelo propuesto.
Se señala que el análisis pueda llevarse a cabo con el modelo propuesto.
questions.answer: Se señala que el análisis puede llevarse a cabo con el modelo propuesto.
questions.rationale: An affirmative reporting verb takes the indicative (puede), the phrase is spelled a cabo, and impersonal se with a que-clause stays singular (se señala).

questions.prompt: Which of the three classical appeals corresponds to the credibility or character of the speaker?
choices: Logos appeals to reason and evidence.
Ethos appeals to the speaker's credibility.
Pathos appeals to the audience's emotions.
Kairos appeals to the timeliness of the argument.
questions.answer: Ethos appeals to the speaker's credibility.
